sources.entry: Dantrolene - Stops the screen from locking while on your home WiFi; locks normally on every other network.

summary.one_liner: Dantrolene is a macOS menu-bar app that keeps the Mac from locking while connected to a chosen Wi-Fi network, and restores normal locking on other networks.
summary.what_it_does: The app keeps the Mac unlocked while it is on a Wi-Fi network the user selects as "home," while still dimming the display after inactivity. Leaving that network restores normal screen locking. It offers Home-network, Always On, and Off modes, and the network is chosen from the menu-bar house icon via "Choose… → Set as Home." The GitHub edition controls the real display and keyboard backlight and supports closed-lid holds through Adrafinil. The App Store edition is sandboxed and dims the display with black overlay windows instead, leaving the panel lit. The README also offers launch at login and a Homebrew cask install.
use_cases: keep Mac unlocked at home while dimming the screen
prevent screen lock on a trusted Wi-Fi network
dim display during inactivity on a Mac
automatic screen lock only away from home Wi-Fi
control keyboard and display backlight on macOS
notable: Locks normally on any network other than the chosen home Wi-Fi
Real display and keyboard backlight control in the GitHub edition
App Store edition is sandboxed and uses black overlay windows for dimming
Closed-lid holds via Adrafinil in the GitHub edition
Home-network, Always On, and Off modes
caveats: Requires macOS 26 or later and Location Services permission to read the Wi-Fi name
A copied Wi-Fi name can trigger the hold; the setting does not authenticate the network
App Store edition cannot control the real backlight; it uses black overlays instead
